summary.headline: Poly Medicure Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 21% YoY to INR534 crore; FY27 consolidated guidance INR2,300-2,400 crore with margin pressure from raw-material costs.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue was INR443 crore (up 5.2% YoY, a record quarter) with standalone EBITDA margin of 27.3%, and consolidated revenue was INR534 crore (up about 21% YoY) with consolidated EBITDA of INR112 crore. FY26 consolidated revenue grew 12.3% to INR1,875 crore, while standalone grew about 4% to INR1,662 crore and standalone EBITDA margin came in at 26.8%. Management flagged a raw-material cost increase of about 20% linked to crude, plus freight and wage pressure, and said gross margin could fall to roughly 66% (200-300 bps lower) on current conditions. FY27 guidance calls for consolidated revenue of INR2,300-2,400 crore and standalone of INR1,900-1,950 crore, with capex of INR200-225 crore.

segments.name: Standalone business
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,662 crore (up about 4%) with 60-70% export-driven; Q4 standalone revenue INR443 crore. Standalone gross margin 68.1% for FY26.

segments.name: Infusion Therapy
segments.commentary: Share of Q4 FY26 revenue fell to 50% from 57% a year earlier; management says it will stay around 50% as the core business, with IV catheter global market share of about 11%.

segments.name: Renal
segments.commentary: About 450 dialysis machines placed in FY26, taking installed base to about 1,000; Renal is about 11% of revenue and Q4 Renal revenue grew about 25% QoQ per an analyst. FY27 Renal growth target is over 20%, versus earlier 30-35%.

segments.name: Cardiology and critical care
segments.commentary: About 11,000 stents deployed in FY26. Stent business is only about INR10-12 crore of revenue; focus is on drug-eluting balloons and other higher-value devices. Management did not disclose cardio and onco revenue.

segments.name: Acquired subsidiaries (Citieffe and PendraCare)
segments.commentary: Combined FY25 revenue about EUR25.5 million (Citieffe about EUR17.5 million, PendraCare about EUR8 million). Citieffe FY27 growth guided at 10-12% in EUR; PendraCare guidance restricted due to Middle East exposure. Steady-state EBITDA margin expected mid-teens, rising to 18-20% over 2-3 years.

segments.name: Brazil (Medyneo acquisition)
segments.commentary: Small acquisition of a company with ANVISA and import licences, about USD40,000 cash outlay; saves an estimated 18-24 months of approval time. The company has no current operations.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance INR2,300-2,400 crore (vs INR1,875 crore in FY26), including full-year consolidation of PendraCare and Citieffe.
FY27 standalone revenue guidance INR1,900-1,950 crore: domestic growth above 20% and international growth above 15%.
FY27 standalone EBITDA margin guidance 25-27%; consolidated EBITDA margin guidance 23-25% because subsidiaries run at lower margins.
Gross margin may erode from about 68% toward about 66% (200-300 bps lower) on current crude and freight conditions; management expects this to ease if crude softens and cost-saving projects deliver.
FY27 capex guidance INR200-225 crore, lower than FY26 INR296 crore.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR296 crore across Haridwar, Faridabad, Mitrol and YEIDA Medical Park; FY27 capex guided at INR200-225 crore with more spend on automation to offset wage increases.
Gamma plant established this year and now fully operational, contributing savings.
Capacity utilisation after QIP-1 capacity expansion is about 65-70%.
Renal installed base about 1,000 dialysis machines after about 450 placements in FY26; management expects about 20% sequential growth in machine sales in FY27.
Clinical registry for a 2,000-patient study: over 650 enrolled; full enrolment targeted by end of FY27 across India and abroad.
demand_pricing: Standalone price increases of 3-5% already taken with customers to offset freight and wage costs.
Raw material costs up about 20% in aggregate (crude-linked, including plastic packaging); raw materials are about 32-33% of revenue. Inventory of 2.5-3 months cushioned Q4 impact.
West Asia disruption: about 6-8% of revenue from the region; demand described as intact, but shipments are delayed by logistics bottlenecks.

Europe: management says demand has recovered over the last 3-4 months after over-inventory and slowdown; distributors added in Northern Europe, UK and Germany. Management targets about 15% growth in Europe.
US: business is recovering after a tariff-related setback that delayed launches by about a year; some new FDA-approved products are in the pipeline.

Chinese dumping in renal and other segments continues; the company is seeking government action (counter-duties and ASEAN duty-free imports). Management says 20-25% growth is still attainable in renal.
Export receivables rose because the company extended better credit terms to international customers to support volumes; management expects receivable cycle similar in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Brazil acquisition's category, revenue and cost, and what is the EU vs RoW split of PendraCare and Citieffe?
qa_highlights.answer: Brazil target is a small, non-operating medical-device storage and distribution company acquired for about USD40,000, saving 18-24 months. Citieffe and PendraCare are each about 50% Europe and 50% RoW; Citieffe also has about 35-40% in North America and Mexico.

qa_highlights.question: Is the renal segment facing Chinese or domestic competition, and what growth is targeted for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said competition is from imports, not domestic players. Renal growth target for FY27 is about 20%, versus an earlier 30-35%, because of Chinese competition and cost inversion.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone inventory and receivables rise sharply, and will they normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone inventory rose about INR30 crore, with finished goods around INR30-35 crore (5-6 days). Receivable days rose from 68 to 86 mainly because of international customers, and management expects a similar cycle in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 gross margin dip QoQ despite growth in higher-margin products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the Q4 dip to product mix, with some lower-margin products in the portfolio.

qa_highlights.question: What is the one-time INR9 crore cost and what was the acquired businesses' EBITDA impact?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR9 crore was transaction-related adviser costs and regulatory and employee provisions booked at year-end at international entities; no manpower rationalisation. The acquired entities had a negative EBITDA impact of about INR2.6 crore in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable organic growth rate and the long-term revenue mix target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited FY27 guidance of over 25% consolidated growth and 15-16% standalone growth. Long-term target is about one-third India and two-thirds RoW.

risks_watch: Raw-material inflation (about 20%) and possible standalone gross margin erosion to about 66% if crude stays at $100-110; management will review at end of Q1 FY27.
West Asia disruption affecting about 6-8% of revenue and shipping, with pending orders not yet executed.
Export receivable days (86) and inventory days (58) elevated; management expects no near-term normalisation.
Chinese import dumping in renal and other segments; Government response (counter-duties, ASEAN duty-free imports) is pending.
Acquired-entity integration: PendraCare exposed to the Middle East; Citieffe lost a Latam tender in CY25; consolidated EBITDA guided lower than standalone.
Brazil entry and US product launches depend on regulatory approvals; import registrations take 6-9 months.
key_quotes: So on the current situation based on where we are today as on today, we may see some erosion on gross margin going from, let's say, 68% to maybe around 66% or maybe in that region, maybe lower by 200 bps, 300 bps.
I can say that absolutely for the moment, yes, but we don't know what can happen tomorrow. That is my worry.
I think we have to see that last year was more or less for us also a lot of transition year because there was a lot of focus on high technology, building new technology products.
Export, in fact, were negative, not flattish also. We were, I think, minus 3% or 4% on the export side.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand recovery in Europe, US and India, and on FY27 guidance, while cautious on raw-material and crude-linked margin risk, West Asia logistics and Chinese dumping in renal. Management repeatedly hedged margin outlook as "very fluid" and dependent on crude softening.

adds.what: Renal dialysis machine placements (about 450 in FY26; installed base about 1,000), expecting ~20% sequential growth in machine sales in FY27

growth.why: FY27 consolidated revenue guided at INR2,300-2,400 crore vs INR1,875 crore (about 22% midpoint, helped by full-year acquisitions), standalone INR1,900-1,950 crore; delivery backed by 3-5% price increases, Europe and domestic growth targets, and Gamma plant, but only partly quantified, with utilisation at 65-70% and gross margin guided down to about 66%.
